preregistration.question: At the anchor date (11 days before a scheduled FOMC meeting), do compact, theory-driven macro variables measured in REAL TIME add information about the decision (Cut/Hold/Hike) beyond a yield-curve market proxy and the policy state?
preregistration.metric: multiclass log loss, probabilities floored at PROB_FLOOR
preregistration.sample: scheduled meetings in the walk-forward out-of-sample window whose target upper bound on the as-of date was above ZLB_UPPER (ex-ZLB)
preregistration.data: ALFRED vintages as of D; release-rule fallback only before a series' first vintage (flagged)
preregistration.test: Diebold-Mariano: mean per-meeting log-loss difference, Newey-West HAC (HAC_LAGS), two-sided
preregistration.decision_rule: p < alpha and treatment better -> 'macro adds information'; p < alpha and treatment worse -> 'macro hurts out of sample'; otherwise 'no detectable difference'
reported_not_decisive: same test on ALL out-of-sample meetings incl. ZLB
circular block bootstrap CI of the mean difference (block BOOT_BLOCK)
secondary: S1 turning points: same two models at reversals / restarts / pauses; P(actual outcome) at the turn and lead time; sign test over episodes; reported as case studies
S2a surprises (replication): does real-time info known the day before the meeting predict the RAW Bauer-Swanson MPS? Expanding-window OLS vs zero forecast, Clark-West one-sided, alpha 0.10
S2b surprises (extension): same, with info as of the 11-day anchor (pre-blackout)
